text.p: Kenny Dalglish is to succeed Kevin Keegan as manager of Newcastle United.
The announcement was made by club chairman Sir John Hall at a specially called news conference at St James' Park on Tuesday.
It is the second time in his career that Dalglish, 45, has replaced Keegan in a key position. In 1977 he took his place in the Liverpool team following Keegan's transfer to Hamburg.
Dalglish, the former Liverpool and Blackburn manager, was working as a scout for Scottish champions Glasgow Rangers when he was approached to take over at St James' Park.

Newcastle are still in with a realistic chance of winning the title for the first time since 1927. They are currently fourth in the table, just five points behind leaders Liverpool and with a match in hand.

If Dalglish does succeed in bringing the championship to Newcastle he would become the first manager to win the English title with three different clubs following three successes with Liverpool in 1986, 1988 and 1990 and Blackburn in 1995.
